findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the Approach and AC1 on the exact set of statuses that require the explicit flag — either enumerate all non-closed statuses in the Approach, or change AC1 to match 'open/in_progress' — so the implementation target is unambiguous.

findings.finding: The Approach section uses 'open/in_progress' as the set of tickets requiring an explicit flag, while AC1 uses 'non-closed tickets'. If the ticket status space includes statuses beyond {open, in_progress, closed} (e.g., 'review', 'blocked', 'paused'), the Approach would silently process those tickets by default while AC1 requires a flag for them — the implementation target is ambiguous.
scenarios: A ticket in 'review' status carries an in-flight claim; the script (following the Approach wording) processes it by default, invalidating the attestation — exactly the harm the guard was meant to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, replace 'open/in_progress ones' with 'non-closed tickets (any status other than closed)' to match AC1's wording, or explicitly enumerate all guarded statuses.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out plan: describe how to restore original ticket descriptions if the live run produces incorrect output or fails mid-batch (e.g., snapshot the pre-migration content per ticket, a --undo mode consuming those snapshots, or a documented manual recovery path via rebar.edit_ticket).
evidence: 'Editing a ticket's description changes its MATERIAL FINGERPRINT, which invalidates any plan-review attestation as stale-material. That is correct and unavoidable'
'NOT a direct rewrite of the git-backed store'
'Run as a dry-run first, with the diff recorded on this ticket before the live run'
ABSENCE: no section describes how to revert a completed or partial live run
findings.finding: The plan acknowledges the migration is destructive (invalidates MATERIAL FINGERPRINTs, overwrites closed-ticket history) and justifies that choice, but provides no rollback or back-out mechanism. The only safety net described is a dry-run diff recorded as a comment, which is pre-migration verification, not reversal. If the live run produces corrupt output or a partial failure mid-batch, there is no described path to undo the changes. The plan explicitly states the changes go through rebar.edit_ticket (not a direct git rewrite), so git revert is not available as an implicit escape hatch.
scenarios: Live run processes 80 of 108 tickets then fails; the 80 already-edited tickets now have invalidated attestations and changed content with no described recovery path.
A bug in the block-rewriting logic produces malformed AC sections; operator needs to restore original content but no rollback procedure exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Before each live edit, record the original description (e.g., in a local JSON snapshot file keyed by ticket ID). Add a `--rollback` mode to the script that re-applies the original descriptions via rebar.edit_ticket, and document this in the plan under a 'Rollback' subsection.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/recovery path to the plan: either a reverse script (`--undo` mode that restores descriptions from the last pre-migration event), a documented `git revert` procedure for the tickets branch, or a pre-migration snapshot step — and add a corresponding AC line verifying the back-out path is exercisable.
evidence: 'A migration script under scripts/ performing the rewrite via the rebar library (rebar.edit_ticket) so every change is a normal, auditable ticket event — NOT a direct rewrite of the git-backed store.' — auditability is asserted but reversibility is not.
ABSENCE: no AC line requiring a rollback script, a dry-run-verified reverse operation, or a procedure to restore ticket descriptions from event history.
'closed tickets' historical accuracy is not preserved by rewriting' — data mutation is acknowledged but rollback is not addressed.
DATA LOSS RISK: a buggy rewrite applied to 108 tickets with no recovery path could permanently corrupt all migrated descriptions.
findings.finding: No explicit rollback / back-out path is described for a partial or fully-completed but incorrect migration. The plan relies on rebar.edit_ticket producing 'auditable ticket events', implying prior state is preserved in event history, but provides no recovery procedure (reverse script, git-revert of the tickets branch, or rebar-based restore). findings.location: Approach section / Acceptance Criteria — no rollback AC present
scenarios: Block-rewriting function has an off-by-one bug that drops the last AC item from every ticket — discovered after the live run completes.
The merge-into-existing-AC logic duplicates items for tickets that already had both headings — 108 tickets now have doubled criteria with no automated way to undo.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one AC: '- [ ] A `--rollback` mode (or equivalent documented procedure) exists that can restore all migrated tickets to their pre-migration descriptions; the dry-run pass records per-ticket before/after state sufficient to drive the reverse operation.' Since rebar.edit_ticket events log prior content, the reverse script can fetch the last event before the migration timestamp and reapply the old description.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the live run handles content that has changed since the dry-run snapshot — e.g., require the script to re-diff each ticket immediately before writing and abort/skip-with-warning if the current content diverges from what the dry run saw, or document that `rebar.edit_ticket` provides optimistic-locking and how conflicts are surfaced.
evidence: Plan states: 'Run as a dry-run first, with the diff recorded on this ticket before the live run.' — the word 'before' establishes a deliberate temporal gap between observation and mutation.

No plan text specifies that the live run re-validates ticket content against what was seen in the dry run, nor does it specify whether `rebar.edit_ticket` offers optimistic-locking or content-hash guards.
The plan does not describe what the script does if `rebar.edit_ticket` returns a conflict error (e.g., abort and report, or overwrite silently).
findings.finding: The plan prescribes a two-phase workflow — dry-run first, diff recorded as a ticket comment, then live run — but specifies no mechanism to detect whether ticket content has changed between the two phases. This is a check-then-act (TOCTOU) race: if any ticket (even a closed one) is edited in the window between the dry-run snapshot and the live run, `rebar.edit_ticket` will silently apply the migration to the modified content, producing an outcome that differs from the previewed diff with no warning to the operator.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Run as a dry-run first, with the diff recorded on this ticket before the live run.' / AC line 5: 'The dry-run diff and the list of skipped in-flight tickets are recorded as comments on this ticket.'
scenarios: An operator records the dry-run diff on Monday and runs the live migration on Tuesday; a colleague has since re-opened and edited a closed ticket's description. The live run migrates the newer content, producing a different result than previewed, with no indication of the divergence.
A CI job or automated process touches a ticket between dry-run and live run; the operator's previewed diff is now stale but the script proceeds without surfacing the discrepancy.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a per-ticket pre-write check: re-read the ticket's current description hash/fingerprint and compare it to the value captured during the dry run; if they differ, skip the ticket, emit a warning listing it, and include its name in the skipped-ticket report rather than proceeding silently.
